newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil state battles to sell bank - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil state battles to sell bank - paper.

text.p: Brazil's Sao Paulo state said it is finding it "impossible" to privatise troubled state bank Banespa due to a lack of interested buyers, a local newspaper said.
Gazeta Mercantil, quoting Finance Secretary Yoshiaki Nakano, said state officials have spoken with 21 large foreign and local financial institutions and none are interested in buying the bank.
Banespa has been under special temporary Central Bank administration for 22 months, the paper said.

Sao Paulo Gov. Mario Covas said he will concede to Banespa's privatisation, not as a premise to an accord with the Central Bank to refinance the state's 20 billion-real debt to the bank, but as an option afterward, the paper said.
"I'll have to end up giving in," he was quoted as saying. "But they just can't demand a total and absolute surrender."
Nakano said both the Central Bank and the federal government know it is impossible to sell the bank, even if the state's debt to Banespa is resolved, the paper reported.
He is slated to meet Thursday with Brazilian Finance Ministy Executive Secretary Pedro Parente to renegotiate Sao Paulo's debt to the federal government, Gazeta said.
